llm.summary: The skill mostly matches its stated purpose (a local runtime security tool) but contains a few coherence issues around installation and path naming that you should resolve before trusting it.

dimensions.detail: Name and description (local runtime security/tool-scanning/DLP) match the declared requirements: only python3 and a home directory (~/.openclaw360) for configs/backups. However, the registry metadata says “No install spec” while the SKILL.md includes explicit install commands (pip install from a pinned GitHub commit). Also the scanner’s default scan path uses ~/.openclaw/skills/ (missing '360'), which looks like an inconsistent path/name and may be a typo or indicate mixed product assumptions.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to run local commands (openclaw360 CLI), read target Skill SKILL.md and script files for static scanning, and read/write only under ~/.openclaw360/. It also enforces strict, single-run scanning and a rigid report template and language rules. Those constraints are plausible for a security skill, but the rigid one-shot/report-template rules are operationally restrictive and should be confirmed as intentional.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill is instruction-only in the registry (no install spec), yet SKILL.md contains a metadata.install section that tells users to run pip3 install git+https://github.com/...@<commit> (and an alternative venv install). Downloading from GitHub at a pinned commit is common, but the mismatch between the registry (no install) and SKILL.md (explicit remote install) is an incoherence to clarify. The install is networked and will write a venv under the user home if the alternative is chosen.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No environment variables or external credentials are requested. Required config paths are limited to ~/.openclaw360/ (config, identity keys, audit, backups). Key usage is local (Ed25519 for signing manifests/logs). This is proportionate to a local security/audit tool.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Top-level disable-model-invocation is true and always:false, so the skill will not be invoked autonomously and does not demand permanent global presence. It writes only to its own ~/.openclaw360/ directory and does not claim to change other skills or system-wide configs.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be a local security tool and mostly behaves consistently with that purpose, but clarify a few things before installing: (1) Confirm the install flow — the registry lists no install spec but SKILL.md tells you to pip install from GitHub (pinned commit). Review the exact commit hash on the repository before running pip install. (2) Confirm the directory naming: SKILL.md refers to ~/.openclaw360 for its own data but the default scan path is listed as ~/.openclaw/skills/ (missing '360') — ask the author whether that is intentional. (3) Inspect the GitHub repo at the pinned commit to verify there is indeed no telemetry, that audit logs are handled as described, and to confirm the code will not make network calls at runtime. (4) Verify the Ed25519 key handling: ensure keys remain local, with permissions set correctly (0600). If you cannot inspect the pinned commit yourself, treat the pip install as higher risk. These mismatches are suspicious but not obviously malicious.
